text: {subject} heard me out and turned one hand palm up. “That doesn’t touch anything I told you.”
{subject} listened to all of it without looking up. “That doesn’t touch anything I told you.”

{subject} heard {place} and {time} and did not seem to mind either one. “That doesn’t touch anything I told you.”
{subject} looked at me a moment, then at the notebook. “That doesn’t touch anything I told you.”
Half an hour was gone, and nothing I knew about {subject} had moved. I had spent worse half hours, but not many.
I laid the fact beside {subject}’s account in the notebook. They did not cross anywhere, and it had cost me half an hour to see it.
I had put the wrong page to {subject}. The half hour was spent all the same, and nobody gives those back.
I wrote nothing new under {subject}’s name. There was nothing new to write.
I closed the notebook. {subject}’s evening was the same evening it had been when I sat down. Mine was shorter.
The fact was about {place}, and {subject} had never told me a word about {place}. I had spent the half hour anyway.
{subject} looked at the notebook, then at the wall behind me, and took {their} time.
{subject} set down what {they} had been holding and wiped {their} hands, each one in turn.
When I said {time}, {subject} stopped. It was a while before {they} started again.
{subject} laughed once, at nothing in particular, and sat up straighter.
{subject} took out a cigarette, did not light it, and put it away again.
{subject} rubbed the side of {their} jaw and looked at the table.
I wrote it down under the first story. {subject} had given me two evenings for the same hours now, and there was only one {subject} to spend them.
I wrote the new words beside the old ones. A person can be in one place a half hour, and now {subject} had given me two.
I drew a line from the first story to the second and wrote {subject}’s name beside both.
I did not argue with {subject}. I read the new story back, and {subject} said that was how it went.
I had two stories from {subject} now, one above the other. I left them there and thought about which one the others fit.
I turned the page. {subject}’s second story about {place} would have to face everything else in the notebook, the way the first one had.
{subject} gave me a long look, then took up again whatever {they} had been doing.
{subject} folded {their} hands and looked down at them. The hands had nothing to say either.
{subject} turned away and found something else to look at. Anything else.
When I said {place}, {subject}’s mouth closed into a flat line.
{subject} took a breath, held it, and let it out again.
{subject} stared past me at the wall and stayed that way. The wall was a very ordinary one.
I waited. {subject} did not fill the silence, and after a time I stopped expecting it.
I wrote {subject}’s name and a dash after it. That was all there was to write.
I left the question with {subject} and got up. The half hour was gone.
Nothing new went into the notebook under {subject}. I made a small mark so I would know I had asked.
{subject} had stopped talking, and silence is not something you can write down. I closed the notebook.
I looked at {subject} a little longer than was polite, and then I let it go.
{subject} let {their} shoulders down, which {they} had not done since I came in.
{subject} let out a long breath, with most of the evening in it, and looked at the floor.
For a while {subject} said nothing. Then {subject} sat back.
{subject} took off {their} hat and turned it around in {their} hands, all the way round, twice.
{subject} looked around to see who else could hear.
When I read out {time}, {subject} closed {their} eyes for a second.
I wrote down where {subject} said {they} had been and what {they} had been doing there. Then I read back what else I had for that hour.
It was a different evening from the one {subject} had given me first. I put it in the notebook in {subject}’s own words and said nothing about it.
I wrote it down word for word. {subject} watched me do it and did not ask me to change anything.
I had {place} from {subject} now, in {subject}’s own words. I would have to find out what else that touched.
I turned the notebook around so {subject} could read what I had written. {subject} read it and nodded, and was kind enough not to mention my handwriting.
I put the pencil away. What {subject} had kept back was in the notebook now, and it had a place and an hour.
{subject} did not look away from me, and did not take long.
{subject} leaned toward me before I had finished.
{subject} nodded while I read it, the whole way through.
{subject} kept on with what {they} had been doing until I finished, and a little after.
{subject} looked at the notebook and then straight back at me.
When I said {place}, {subject} did not blink. I did enough blinking for the pair of us.
It was the same evening {subject} had given me before. I wrote that down, and left the fact I had brought one line above it.
{subject} had not changed a word of the first story. I wrote that down and turned the page.
I wrote down that {subject} had kept to it. The fact I had read out was still in the notebook too.
Nothing I had on {subject} changed. Both things were still written down, the story and the fact.
I looked at the notebook for a while after {subject} finished. Then I closed it and left it the way it was.
{subject} had said it twice now, the same way both times. I wrote the second time under the first.
{subject} looked at the floor for a long time.
{subject} opened {their} mouth, shut it, and started again.
{subject} looked at me, then at the notebook in my hand, and swallowed.
When I said {time}, {subject} looked away over my shoulder.
{subject} rubbed {their} eyes with the heel of one hand.
{subject} sat very still, both hands in {their} lap.
I drew a line through the word “together” under {subject}’s name. It had been {subject}’s word to give, and {subject} had taken it back.
I wrote down what {subject} had said. Somebody else’s evening had one name fewer in it now.
{subject} had given somebody a half hour earlier in the night, and now {subject} had taken it back. I wrote it down the way {subject} said it.
In {subject}’s first story there had been two people. Now there was only {subject}.
I thanked {subject} and did not press. The other name in that story would need somebody else to speak for it, or nobody.
I read the page back for a while. The words that had put {subject} beside somebody else were no good any more.
{subject} shook {their} head before I had finished. “That’s all I’m going to say about it.”
{subject} glanced past me at the door. “That’s all I’m going to say about it.”
{subject} heard it through and folded {their} hands. “That’s all I’m going to say about it.”
{subject} let out a breath and sat back. “That’s all I’m going to say about it.”
{subject} didn’t look at the notebook this time. “That’s all I’m going to say about it.”
{subject} waited to be sure I was done. “That’s all I’m going to say about it.”
I let it go. What {subject} had told me last was still what {subject} had told me, and it had cost me nothing more to find that out.
I closed the notebook on it. {subject}’s story stood where {subject} had left it, for now.
That was all of it for tonight. The first thing I had read out touched {subject}’s story, and the second had not.
I didn’t push {subject}. The story was the same story, and the second thing I had read out was no use against it.
I put the pencil back. If there was a second thing that crossed {subject}’s story, it was not the one I had just read.
{subject} was done, and so was I, for the moment. Nothing new went under {subject}’s name.
